Project journal
Experiments and evidence

text.name: Article title
text.text: Guides

text.name: Description
text.text: Follow the project from its first screen change to original firmware, audio and the work still on the bench.

text.name: Title
text.text: Our first change on the SP.

text.name: Description
text.text: Follow the first visible firmware change in seven steps, with the original evidence, animated diagrams and an offline Python exercise.

text.name: Title
text.text: Getting pad information onto the screen

text.name: Description
text.text: A working text renderer still needs a route from the real screen. R2 taught us to test both.

text.name: Title
text.text: Making AntiWorkProTwerk move

text.name: Description
text.text: The first working animation joined an integer renderer, owned widget state and the screen's existing redraw callback.

text.name: Title
text.text: Building a diagnostic capture we could trust

text.name: Description
text.text: A failed task, a corrected stack and the checks behind our first useful boot-region capture.

text.name: Title
text.text: Our first original application

text.name: Description
text.text: What R6 and R7 established about starting our own code, drawing a screen and responding to the power switch.

text.name: Title
text.text: Giving every control a name

text.name: Description
text.text: From moving bars to 55 accepted mappings, with one control at a time and the raw recordings kept for review.

text.name: Title
text.text: Turning raw readings into usable controls

text.name: Description
text.text: Put the accepted map into an original event decoder, then separate knob acquisition, event filtering and visible movement.

text.name: Title
text.text: From a RAM upload to a booted update

text.name: Description
text.text: How a working USB connection became a verified persistent update, with a failed compatibility check in between.

text.name: Title
text.text: A USB writer that survives the update

text.name: Description
text.text: Why installing a working application removed its updater, and how the B1 bridge kept a writer available afterward.

text.name: Title
text.text: What a partial update taught us

text.name: Description
text.text: A cumulative work limit stopped a write partway through. The failure changed how we budget operations and report success.

text.name: Title
text.text: Load, run, return

text.name: Description
text.text: A bounded program ran from RAM and returned to the updater without an owner power cycle. R37 made that round trip observable.

text.name: Title
text.text: When moving counters were not sound

text.name: Description
text.text: How frozen receive windows, corrected comparisons and a known input separated bus activity from changing audio.

text.name: Title
text.text: The timeout that wasn't a stalled stream

text.name: Description
text.text: A first-fault snapshot exposed a timestamp race. R41 then sustained silent streaming, while audible output remained a separate test.

text.name: Title
text.text: Small pieces, tested in isolation

text.name: Description
text.text: How we separated reusable audio code from the board, and checked its behavior before connecting it to hardware.

text.name: Title
text.text: Keeping a way back

text.name: Description
text.text: What our offline loader tests establish, and why replacing reset-time code still needs an independent recovery path.

text.name: Title
text.text: Pitch correction, before the firmware

text.name: Description
text.text: Separating pitch detection, musical decisions and sound processing while keeping latency and evidence in view.

text.name: Title
text.text: A synth that belongs on the SP

text.name: Description
text.text: Designing a live instrument around the pads, knobs and capture workflow, while testing how it could share Roland's sampler.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Each chapter separates device observations, offline checks and open questions. The downloadable exercises use invented data and run without an SP. Research chapters describe work in progress, not released features.
